newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends slightly higher on export, soy gain.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends slightly higher on export, soy gain.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended slightly higher on Friday with gains sparked by a large sale of U.S. corn to unknown destinations and a rally in soybean futures, traders said.

USDA early Friday said 405,000 tonnes of corn were sold to unknown destinations with 165,000 tonnes of 1996-97 delivery and 240,000 tonnes for shipment during the 1997-98 marketing year which begins on September 1.
But gains in new crop December were limited by generally satisfactory crop seeding weather this week in the U.S. Midwest corn growing areas.
Floor sources said corn plantings would jump sharply this week. Traders said Monday's USDA weekly crop report would show the corn crop was 20 to 35 percent seeded.
Commercial firms were sellers of the nearbys on the day which lent credence to ideas farmers planned to seed corn.
Funds were aggressive buyers on the day but trade sources said the moves were short covering. Refco Inc reportedly bought 20 million bushels July corn.
Corn ended 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1/2 cent lower with May up 1-1/2 at $2.94-1/2 and new crop December unchanged at $2.78-1/2.
On the day, Lind Waldock sold 1.5 million July and Rand Financial sold one million December, traders said.

In options trade, Tenco Inc bought 500 July $2.70 puts at 1-7/8 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 400 July $2.50 puts at 3/8 cents and Refco Inc sold 300 December $3.00 calls at 13 to 14 cents, pit sources said.
"Three dollars in the July was a very significant point," one options trader said. "Since futures did not get to $3, (options traders) started looking lower."
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 106,565 contracts.
